harvest.GH418_pooling_caveat: *** REGISTERED, and it revises this file's own arm_note. The launch record justified pooling with 'the three commits land gated ids that are NOT in the armed string'. That criterion is NOT sufficient, and this round's read-the-source check found a real exception: 87bc6b33 (slotdust) also changed an UNGATED line in J.IsClosestToDustLocation -- `if dist < closestDist` became `if dist <= closestDist` (jmz_func.lua:11520), outside every bSlotDust branch, while the comment 20 lines above claims 'Unarmed this is byte-for-byte the shipped function'. Filed as GH #418. Impact is small and one-directional-neutral (it flips WHICH of two exactly-equidistant dust carriers wins a tie; exactly one bot still wins, and the shipped pid/slot bug makes ties structurally impossible on dire), so the pooling STANDS -- but it stands as an explicit reservation, not as the byte-equivalence the launch record claimed. Separately checked and found genuinely inert: 0b468372 (slotarb) edits IsTheClosestOne, the wrapper that ALSO resolves the ARMED id campsel; with bSlotArb false, nSlot = id and the body reduces to the shipped one. That negative is registered here precisely because a check recorded only when it fires is invisible when it passes.
harvest.DC3_illumove_illureal: REGISTERED per test_set.md SS-DC.3 (this wave's harvest obligation). Both `illumove` and `illureal` are armed in the 52-id string, and they are NOT orthogonal within a frame: illureal armed makes more illusions return early at illusions.lua:80, so those units never reach the :94 movement gate and illumove's domain SHRINKS. Consequence for any downstream reader of this corpus: frames in the intersection (non-Naga/PL illusion AND owner <40% HP AND retreating AND not strong) CANNOT have their attribution split between the two ids. Outside that intersection the two do not interact. Nothing in the test suite pins this -- both acceptance tests arm only their own id -- so it is only knowable by reading that line. The readings above are WHOLE-BUNDLE (52-id) readings and make no per-id claim, so nothing recorded here violates the limitation; it binds whoever next tries per-id attribution on this corpus.
